reason: The goal calls for insulated outgoing nerve routes, and the support cells appear able to wrap the motor neuron fibers.
expectation: The support cells will insulate the motor neuron fibers.

effect: The support cells wrapped the motor fibers, creating motor nerves; the next goal is to connect sight to muscle commands.
reaction: The segmented wrapping is a useful detail about how support cells help signals travel.
reason: Sensory nerves appear to carry information from the eyes toward the central nervous system.
expectation: The sensory nerves will connect to the eyes to carry visual information.

effect: The eyes and sensory nerves form a visual information route; it still needs to connect to the system that directs movement.
reaction: The change from light rays to a nerve signal makes the route clearer.
reason: The central nervous system can receive visual information and coordinate muscle commands.
expectation: The visual route will connect to the central nervous system.

effect: The visual route now connects to the brain as a seeing control system; muscle commands still need an outgoing connection.
reaction: The distinction between seeing the target and producing force is clear.
reason: Motor nerves carry outgoing signals, so they are a plausible next connection for the seeing control system.
expectation: The motor nerves will connect the control system to an outgoing route for muscle commands.

effect: The motor nerves connect to the arm first, forming a nerve-linked arm; the seeing control system still needs a connection to it.
reaction: I expected a direct connection to the control system, so the intermediate attachment was a small surprise.
reason: The nerve-linked arm appears ready to connect to the seeing control system for outgoing muscle commands.
expectation: The control system will connect to the arm's motor nerves.

effect: The seeing control system connected to the nerve-linked arm, completing the sight-to-command route; the remaining goal is position feedback.
reaction: The inward and outward arrows make the two signal directions clear.
reason: The stretch receptors and sensory nerves appear suited to carrying information about the arm’s position back to the control system.
expectation: The receptors and sensory nerves will connect to the guided arm to provide position information.

effect: The stretch receptors completed the return route for position information, finishing the chapter.
reaction: The eyes-closed example makes the purpose of position feedback tangible.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the visual route and arm was worthwhile because the inward and outward arrows brought sensing and muscle commands together in one diagram.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the visual route felt fairly predictable, though the distinction between light and a nerve signal helped explain it.

surprise.text: I expected the motor nerves to connect directly to the seeing control system, but they attached to the arm first.

arbitrary.text: That required attachment order was not obvious to me, although the resulting connection to muscle fibers had a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the guided arm works in the wider body. The position-feedback example made the connections feel relevant, though most choices were predictable.
